messages.author: 17c61d3201bc8acf
messages.subject: Suggested Stable Environment?
parts:
I have been trying to get Rhipe installed against CDH5, using the rearch branch from Git and from our thread yesterday have it relatively close, but still no luck.

Can you tell me the recommended stable environment to run, IE. CDH 4.6, R 3-1.0, protocol buffers 2.4, etc?

Also, I am a bit confused between the MRv1 and MRv2, if you could help me understand the best way to set this up within the above suggested environment (IE, only install MapReduc, not YARN, etc).

Thanks!
Luke.

messages.subject: Fwd: [rhipe] Suggested Stable Environment?

Hadoop (the new Hadoop) can be started as MRv1 (using old style) or

work (the

For RHIPE to work on MRv2, the job history server must be running.
That said, it hasn't been tested.

Regards
Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Suggested Stable Environment?
parts:
I would prefer to get it running CDH5, but at this point I have tried both CDH5 and CDH4 and ended in the same error (java.io.IOException: Stream Closed, from earlier thread).

Here is what I did yesterday:

  - Setup 2 new VM's running CentOS 6.2, and installed CDH 4.6 (using Cloudera Manager).
  - Verified that I was able to run haddop jar hadoop-examples.jar pi 10 100, and it ran successfully within the MRv1 Job Tracker.
  - Installed R 3.1.0
  - Started R, and ran install.packages("rJava")
  - Downloaded pb 2.4.1 (this is the only place I see a diff), compiled and installed via make
  - Downloaded Rhipe_0.74.0.tar.gz, and ran R CMD INSTALL Rhip_0.74.0.tar.gz

Everything seemed to run successfully, and when I start R, I have no problems with library(Rhipe) and rhinit().

I get the seg-fault when I run the following, even on the new machines with CDH4.6:

RHIPEWHAT=0 R CMD /usr/local/lib64/R/library/Rhipe/bin/RhipeMapReduce --slave --silent --vanilla

I feel like I am so close to getting it work, and just can't quite get it to work in a clustered environment (I was able to get it to work with CDH5 in single node mode by downloading the CDH5 tar ball and starting it manually).  Do you have any ideas where I could focus my troubleshooting efforts?  I feel like I need to get the RHIPEWHAT command to run without seg-faulting, but am not sure where to start.

Thanks again for all your help/input!
Luke.

parts:
My fault, it will segfault. Try this

rhipe_outputformat_class="org.apache.hadoop.mapreduce.lib.output.NullOutputFormat"
rhipe_map_bytes_read=1000 rhipe_map_buff_size=1000 io_sort_mb=10
rhipe_combiner=0 RHIPEWHAT=10 R CMD ~/R_LIBS/Rhipe/bin/RhipeMapReduce
--slave --silent --vanilla

change your paths accordingly. You should get Bad value for RHIPEWHAT: 10

And if you change RHIPEWHAT=0, it should just wait.

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Suggested Stable Environment?
parts:
Definitely permissions. RHIPE calls freopen to open standard output in binary mode ("wb"). However this might fail on some systems - i dont know which. Definitely not RHEL 5, Ubuntu, OS X.

Save this code as testopen.c

#include <errno.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdio.h>

int main(int argc, char **argv){
  printf("Trying to reopen standard output in 'wb' mode\n");
  FILE *fp = freopen(NULL,"wb", stdout);
  if(!fp){
    printf("Error reopening: %s\n", strerror(errno));
    return(errno);
  }
  printf("All okay\n");
  return(0);
}
   
And then compile : cc -otest testopen.c
and run: ./test

What output?
